title: RFM-Net: A Convolutional Neural Network for Customer Segment Classification
tldr: RFM-Net fuses Recency-Frequency-Monetary analysis with a lightweight convolutional neural network to classify customers into seven behavioral segments, achieving 94.33% accuracy on a real-world retail dataset.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional RFM-based segmentation relies on rule-based logic that cannot capture nonlinear patterns in customer behavior. Statistical and clustering methods provide static groupings lacking adaptability in dynamic markets. A more robust, intelligent, and scalable segmentation technique is needed.
approach: Proposed RFM-Net, a hybrid framework combining RFM analysis with a custom CNN for customer segment classification.
Raw transactional data are preprocessed, aggregated per customer, and transformed into Recency, Frequency, and Monetary metrics.
Continuous RFM metrics are discretized into 1-5 scores using user-defined thresholds, then mapped to seven predefined segment labels via rule-based logic.
A shallow CNN architecture with two convolutional layers, max-pooling, and a softmax output layer classifies customers into segments.
The model uses only three input features (R, F, M) with 6,823 total trainable parameters, ensuring computational efficiency.
Evaluation employed 10-fold cross-validation on the UCI Online Retail dataset (541,909 records) with accuracy, precision, recall, and F-measure metrics.
A comprehensive sensitivity analysis examined convolutional layers, learning rate, filter count, k-fold count, and RFM threshold configurations.
RFM-Net was compared against 14 prior methods on the same dataset and seven baseline ML models under identical experimental conditions.
A second validation was performed on the Online Retail II dataset (1,067,371 records) to confirm generalizability.
Permutation feature importance analysis was conducted to assess the relative contribution of each RFM variable to classification.
findings: num: RFM-Net achieved 94.33% classification accuracy on the primary Online Retail dataset.
num: A relative average increase of 13.17% in accuracy was observed compared to previously reported results on the same dataset.
num: On the Online Retail II dataset, RFM-Net achieved 95.41% accuracy, confirming generalizability.
num: The model uses only 6,823 trainable parameters (approximately 26.65 KB), making it lightweight and efficient.
num: Recency was identified as the most important feature with a permutation importance score of 0.5358, followed by Frequency (0.4217) and Monetary (0.2642).
num: Two convolutional layers yielded optimal performance; adding more layers degraded accuracy (e.g., 7 layers dropped to 90.85%).
num: A learning rate of 0.01 achieved peak performance, while higher rates such as 0.04 reduced accuracy to 90.06%.
num: RFM-Net outperformed all seven baseline models, improving accuracy by 6.31 percentage points over the average baseline performance of 88.02%.
Potential Loyalists comprised 23.70% of the customer base, followed by Loyal Customers (18.28%) and Hibernating (17.39%).
Training and validation losses converged after epoch 15, reaching 0.1549 and 0.1502 respectively, indicating stable learning without overfitting.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: General overview of the RFM-Net pipeline from data acquisition to decision-making support -> Demonstrates end-to-end methodology from raw data to actionable insights.
Figure 2: Customer segments grid view based on RFM scores -> Seven behavioral segments mapped onto a recency vs. frequency-monetary grid.
Figure 3: Distribution of customer segments across the dataset -> Potential Loyalists are the largest group at 23.70%.
Figure 4: Permutation feature importance analysis -> Recency dominates at 0.5358, confirming temporal signals as primary classifiers.
Figure 5: Confusion matrix across seven segments -> Potential Loyalists classified at 96.9%, Need Attention at 90.5%.
Figure 6: Training and validation loss over 20 epochs -> Losses converge near epoch 15, confirming generalization.
Table 3: CNN architecture and parameter summary -> Total 6,823 parameters across six layers totaling approximately 26.65 KB.
Table 7: 10-fold cross-validation performance -> Accuracy ranges from 90.78% to 97.23% with an average of 94.33%.
Table 9: Comparative results against 14 prior methods -> RFM-Net surpasses all methods including PARM (90.00%) and Random Forest (87.60%).
Table 10: Baseline ML model comparison -> RFM-Net exceeds MLP (85.50%), KNN (92.39%), and Bagging DT (90.68%).

key_equations.explanation: Recency calculated as days since a customer's most recent purchase relative to the latest dataset date.
Frequency is the count of distinct invoices for customer c.
Monetary value is the sum of all purchase amounts for customer c.

definitions.definition: Recency, Frequency, and Monetary — three behavioral metrics quantifying customer engagement and value.
Convolutional Neural Network — a deep learning architecture using convolutional filters for pattern extraction.
The proposed lightweight CNN architecture that classifies customers into behavioral segments using RFM features as input.
Factor Analysis of Mixed Data — a dimensionality reduction technique for datasets with both numerical and categorical variables.
Area Under the Curve — a threshold-insensitive metric for evaluating binary classification performance.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: RFM-Net contributes a lightweight CNN architecture specifically designed for structured behavioral data classification, demonstrating that shallow convolutional models can outperform both traditional ML baselines and deeper networks on low-dimensional tabular inputs. The paper establishes that combining domain-driven feature engineering (RFM) with data-driven learning produces robust classification with minimal parameters (6,823). The comprehensive sensitivity analysis across multiple hyperparameter dimensions provides methodological guidance for CNN-based classification on structured data. The dual-dataset validation confirms the approach generalizes across different retail transaction scales.
directly_justifies: RFM-Net achieves 94.33% classification accuracy on real-world retail transactional data using only three input features.
A relative average accuracy increase of 13.17% over prior methods on the same dataset demonstrates significant improvement.
Recency is the most important predictive feature with a permutation importance score of 0.5358.
A shallow CNN with two convolutional layers outperforms seven baseline ML models by 6.31 percentage points.
Generalization confirmed on Online Retail II dataset with 95.41% accuracy across 1,067,371 records.
limits: Customer segment labels are generated from predefined RFM rules, introducing circularity into the supervised training framework.
The Online Retail dataset originates from a single UK-based retailer, limiting demonstrated generalizability to other industries and regions.
Only three input features are used, potentially constraining the model's ability to capture richer behavioral patterns beyond RFM.
No real-time or deployment evaluation was conducted, leaving practical deployment considerations unaddressed.

limitations: Customer segment labels are generated from predefined RFM rules and used as ground truth for CNN training, introducing circularity [unacknowledged].
The study uses only the UCI Online Retail dataset from a single UK-based retailer, limiting generalizability to other industries, regions, and data distributions.
Only three RFM features are used as model inputs, potentially constraining the capture of richer behavioral patterns beyond recency, frequency, and monetary value.
No real-time deployment or production evaluation was conducted, leaving practical scalability and real-world deployment considerations unaddressed.
The rule-based threshold values for RFM discretization were determined through empirical experimentation rather than principled optimization, introducing a degree of subjectivity.
remember_this: RFM-Net combines RFM analysis with a lightweight CNN achieving 94.33% accuracy on customer segment classification.
The model uses only 6,823 parameters and three input features while outperforming all compared baselines.
Recency is the dominant predictive feature with a permutation importance of 0.5358.
Generalization was confirmed on a second dataset with 95.41% accuracy across over one million records.
Deeper CNN configurations degraded performance, confirming that shallow architectures are optimal for low-dimensional structured data.
